topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently

sections.title: The Familiar Intuition: Real Convergence
lecture_lines: In Euclidean space, smaller steps equal smaller distance.
Example: A squirrel approaching a nut via halves.
The sequence converges as terms approach zero.
animations: Fade in the real number line background #FFFFFF [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/squirrel.svg].
Highlight the decreasing distance to zero #FF00FF.

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
lecture_lines: The 2-adic norm measures divisibility by two.
Numbers are close if their difference is divisible.
High power of two means smaller 2-adic distance.
animations: Display the integers 10 and 2 in binary form using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg] #FFFFFF.
Animate the subtraction result with trailing zeros highlighted #FF0000.
Display the calculated 2-adic distance as 2 to the negative power using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/abacus.svg] #00FFFF.

sections.title: Paradoxical Convergence
lecture_lines: Convergence depends on terms shrinking towards zero.
Powers of two shrink in the 2-adic sense.
They converge to zero as exponents grow.
animations: Display powers 2^n for n=1, 2, 3... in a row #FFFFFF.
Show these powers approaching zero in 2-adic distance #00FF00.

sections.title: The Grand Finale: Summing to Infinity
lecture_lines: This geometric series equals negative one.
Binary representation fills with ones indefinitely.
Two's complement arithmetic confirms this result.
animations: Display the infinite series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 +... using an [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/abacus.svg] #FFFFFF.
Final focus on the 2-adic series equivalence using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg] #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Summary and Perspective
lecture_lines: Convergence is relative to your chosen metric.
Euclidean distance measures size; 2-adic measures divisibility.
Mathematics thrives on these different perspectives.
